A.explanation: $4.9 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m} = 4.9 \text{ nm}$, which is in the X-ray region, far shorter than visible light.

B.explanation: $6.6 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m} = 6.6 \text{ nm}$, which is also X-ray or extreme ultraviolet, not visible light.

C.explanation: $5.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 550 \text{ nm}$, which lies in the middle of the visible spectrum where green light occurs.

D.explanation: $8.6 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 860 \text{ nm}$, which is longer than red light and lies in the infrared region.

walkthrough: Recall the order of the electromagnetic spectrum: visible light has wavelengths of a few hundred nanometres, about $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ for violet to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ for red.
Green light is in the middle of the visible range, roughly $500-560 \text{ nm}$, or about $5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Convert the options using $\lambda$ in $\text{nm} = \lambda$ in $\text{m} \div 10^{-9}$: A gives $4.9 \text{ nm}$, B gives $6.6 \text{ nm}$, C gives $550 \text{ nm}$, D gives $860 \text{ nm}$.
Classify them: $4.9 \text{ nm}$ and $6.6 \text{ nm}$ are X-ray wavelengths, and $860 \text{ nm}$ is longer than visible red so is infrared.
Only $5.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 550 \text{ nm}$ falls inside the visible band at the expected green position. This is option C.
